children: Higher oil prices amid Middle East tensions are increasingly feeding into Japan's consumer prices, particularly for daily necessities and durable goods, says NLI Research Institute economist Taro Saito. Inflation for daily essentials such as tissue paper, plastic bags and facial cleansers accelerated for a sixth straight month in October, rising 6.9% from a year earlier, from April's 1.5% gain, according to NLI estimates. "Higher crude oil prices are being passed on to retail prices with a time lag through rising costs for petrochemical products and packaging materials," Saito says. "Inflation for durable consumer goods is also steadily accelerating, driven by rising semiconductor and memory prices amid expanding global AI-related demand," he adds. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
